annotations.text:
RICH MODE — "DAWN"

Warm dark ground, editorial serif for the human parts, mono for every figure. The sun arc tracks the real day. Green is eBird, terracotta and blue are Claude and Codex — borrowed from llmdash's own dark theme so the two apps read as siblings.

Switcher sits top right, beside the arc.

Fixed since the first pass: the bookmarks block no longer overruns the frame (the card row sizes to its content instead of a hard 380px), the weather card distributes its slack so the row has a level bottom edge, and the hairline rules can no longer collapse under pressure.

DATA HONESTY — FIXED

The eBird sparkline was an area chart closing to a zero baseline, which made its May peak imply ~221 species in a month against a 284 year list. Now a line, no implied baseline.

September is 7 days old, so its segment is dashed and its dot hollow — it no longer reads as a settled month.

Red-necked Phalarope came off the rare list: it is expected in the thousands at Alviso in September. Pull this from eBird's notable endpoint, never a hand-kept list.

The headroom line now names both windows — Codex has the 5-hour room, Claude the weekly. The old copy was true on one horizon and false on the other.

TEXT MODE — now a spec, not a sketch

Same four widgets, no cards: a label column and rows of values, everything visible at once. All mono, one family.

It shows MORE than rich mode, not less — seven hourly readings instead of five, both reset countdowns with meters, 21 bookmarks. Density is the point of the mode.

Note it needs 820×620 to say what rich mode needs 1440×900 for.

Known tradeoff, carried over deliberately: 24px link rows are below a comfortable touch target. If a phone ends up on text mode, the rows want to grow at narrow widths.

THE QUESTION ON THE TABLE

Identical markup, two palettes — pick one and the other is a single deletion.

DARK (left) keeps density as the only thing the switcher changes, so light/dark stays a separate axis you can add later on either mode.

LIGHT (right) is the day page to Dawn's night page. Reads better in a bright room, but it welds ground colour to density: choosing text mode would also mean choosing light.

Worth deciding by eye now, because it sets whether the build needs one theme axis or two.
